question.:question/problem: If $f(x,y)=2 x^{2} + 2 x y^{2}$ and $r(t)=\ln{\left(t \right)}\,i+2 e^{t}\,j,$ compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))].$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2 x^{2} + 2 x y^{2})\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(2 x^{2} + 2 x y^{2})\,j \\  & =(4 x + 2 y^{2})\,i+4 x y\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x=\ln{\left(t \right)}$ and $y=2 e^{t}$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =(4(\ln{\left(t \right)})+2(2 e^{t})^{2})\,i+4(\ln{\left(t \right)})(2 e^{t})\,j \\  & =(8 e^{2 t} + 4 \ln{\left(t \right)})\,i+8 e^{t} \ln{\left(t \right)}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\ln{\left(t \right)})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2 e^{t})\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{t}\,i+2 e^{t}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =((8 e^{2 t} + 4 \ln{\left(t \right)})\,i+8 e^{t} \ln{\left(t \right)}\,j)\cdot (\frac{1}{t}\,i+2 e^{t}\,j) \\  & =((8 e^{2 t} + 4 \ln{\left(t \right)}))(\frac{1}{t})+(8 e^{t} \ln{\left(t \right)})(2 e^{t}) \\  & =\frac{4 \ln{\left(t \right)}}{t}+\frac{8 e^{2 t}}{t}+16 e^{2 t} \ln{\left(t \right)} \\  & =16 e^{2 t} \ln{\left(t \right)} + \frac{8 e^{2 t}}{t} + \frac{4 \ln{\left(t \right)}}{t}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\ln{\left(t \right)})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3 e^{t})\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{t}\,i+3 e^{t}\,j.\end{aligned}

question.:question/worked-solution:
The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(4x{y}^{2}))\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(4x{y}^{2}))\,j \\  & =\frac{4(1{y}^{2}+x2y\cdot 0)}{1+16{x}^{2}{y}^{4}}\,i+\frac{4(0{y}^{2}+x2y\cdot 1)}{1+16{x}^{2}{y}^{4}}\,j \\  & =\frac{4{y}^{2}}{1+16{x}^{2}{y}^{4}}\,i+\frac{8xy}{1+16{x}^{2}{y}^{4}}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x={e}^{4t}$ and $y=\operatorname{sin}⁡5t$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =\frac{4(\operatorname{sin}⁡5t)^{2}}{1+16({e}^{4t})^{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡5t)^{4}}\,i+\frac{8({e}^{4t})(\operatorname{sin}⁡5t)}{1+16({e}^{4t})^{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡5t)^{4}}\,j \\  & =\frac{4\sin^{2}⁡5t}{1+16{e}^{8t}\sin^{4}⁡5t}\,i+\frac{8{e}^{4t}\operatorname{sin}⁡5t}{1+16{e}^{8t}\sin^{4}⁡5t}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{4t})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡5t)\,j \\  & =4{e}^{4t}\,i+5\operatorname{cos}⁡5t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =(\frac{4\sin^{2}⁡5t}{1+16{e}^{8t}\sin^{4}⁡5t}\,i+\frac{8{e}^{4t}\operatorname{sin}⁡5t}{1+16{e}^{8t}\sin^{4}⁡5t}\,j)\cdot (4{e}^{4t}\,i+5\operatorname{cos}⁡5t\,j) \\  & =\frac{16{e}^{4t}\sin^{2}⁡5t}{1+16{e}^{8t}\sin^{4}⁡5t}+\frac{40{e}^{4t}\operatorname{sin}⁡5t\operatorname{cos}⁡5t}{1+16{e}^{8t}\sin^{4}⁡5t} \\  & =\frac{4{e}^{4t}(4\sin^{2}⁡5t+10\operatorname{sin}⁡5t\operatorname{cos}⁡5t)}{1+16{e}^{8t}\sin^{4}⁡5t}.\end{aligned}
$$

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: \frac{4 \left(8 e^{8 t} + 5 \sin{\left(5 t \right)} \cos{\left(5 t \right)}\right) \sin{\left(5 t \right)}}{16 e^{8 t} \sin^{4}{\left(5 t \right)} + 1}
\frac{4 \left(2 e^{4 t} + \sin{\left(5 t \right)}\right) \sin{\left(5 t \right)}}{16 e^{8 t} \sin^{4}{\left(5 t \right)} + 1}
\frac{8 \left(2 \sin{\left(5 t \right)} + 5 \cos{\left(5 t \right)}\right) e^{4 t} \sin{\left(5 t \right)}}{16 e^{8 t} \sin^{4}{\left(5 t \right)} + 1}

\frac{16 e^{4 t} \sin^{2}{\left(5 t \right)}}{16 e^{8 t} \sin^{4}{\left(5 t \right)} + 1}

knowledge_point.title: Applying the Vector Form of the Chain Rule to a Function of Two Variables

question.:question/worked-solution:
The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(x{y}^{2}))\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(x{y}^{2}))\,j \\  & =\frac{(1{y}^{2}+x2y\cdot 0)}{1+{x}^{2}{y}^{4}}\,i+\frac{(0{y}^{2}+x2y\cdot 1)}{1+{x}^{2}{y}^{4}}\,j \\  & =\frac{{y}^{2}}{1+{x}^{2}{y}^{4}}\,i+\frac{2xy}{1+{x}^{2}{y}^{4}}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x={e}^{3t}$ and $y=\operatorname{sin}⁡2t$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =\frac{(\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)^{2}}{1+({e}^{3t})^{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)^{4}}\,i+\frac{2({e}^{3t})(\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)}{1+({e}^{3t})^{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)^{4}}\,j \\  & =\frac{\sin^{2}⁡2t}{1+{e}^{6t}\sin^{4}⁡2t}\,i+\frac{2{e}^{3t}\operatorname{sin}⁡2t}{1+{e}^{6t}\sin^{4}⁡2t}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{3t})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)\,j \\  & =3{e}^{3t}\,i+2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =(\frac{\sin^{2}⁡2t}{1+{e}^{6t}\sin^{4}⁡2t}\,i+\frac{2{e}^{3t}\operatorname{sin}⁡2t}{1+{e}^{6t}\sin^{4}⁡2t}\,j)\cdot (3{e}^{3t}\,i+2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,j) \\  & =\frac{3{e}^{3t}\sin^{2}⁡2t}{1+{e}^{6t}\sin^{4}⁡2t}+\frac{4{e}^{3t}\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\operatorname{cos}⁡2t}{1+{e}^{6t}\sin^{4}⁡2t} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{3t}(3\sin^{2}⁡2t+4\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)}{1+{e}^{6t}\sin^{4}⁡2t}.\end{aligned}
$$

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: \frac{2 \left(3 e^{6 t} + \sin{\left(2 t \right)} \cos{\left(2 t \right)}\right) \sin{\left(2 t \right)}}{e^{6 t} \sin^{4}{\left(2 t \right)} + 1}
\frac{\left(2 e^{3 t} + \sin{\left(2 t \right)}\right) \sin{\left(2 t \right)}}{e^{6 t} \sin^{4}{\left(2 t \right)} + 1}
- \frac{\left(- 3 \sin{\left(2 t \right)} + 4 \cos{\left(2 t \right)}\right) e^{3 t} \sin{\left(2 t \right)}}{e^{6 t} \sin^{4}{\left(2 t \right)} + 1}
\frac{\left(3 \sin{\left(2 t \right)} + 4 \cos{\left(2 t \right)}\right) e^{3 t} \sin{\left(2 t \right)}}{e^{6 t} \sin^{4}{\left(2 t \right)} + 1}

$$

$$

$$

knowledge_point.title: Applying the Vector Form of the Chain Rule to a Function of Two Variables

question.:question/worked-solution:
The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(2x{y}^{2}))\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(2x{y}^{2}))\,j \\  & =\frac{2(1{y}^{2}+x2y\cdot 0)}{1+4{x}^{2}{y}^{4}}\,i+\frac{2(0{y}^{2}+x2y\cdot 1)}{1+4{x}^{2}{y}^{4}}\,j \\  & =\frac{2{y}^{2}}{1+4{x}^{2}{y}^{4}}\,i+\frac{4xy}{1+4{x}^{2}{y}^{4}}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x={e}^{2t}$ and $y=\operatorname{sin}⁡4t$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =\frac{2(\operatorname{sin}⁡4t)^{2}}{1+4({e}^{2t})^{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡4t)^{4}}\,i+\frac{4({e}^{2t})(\operatorname{sin}⁡4t)}{1+4({e}^{2t})^{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡4t)^{4}}\,j \\  & =\frac{2\sin^{2}⁡4t}{1+4{e}^{4t}\sin^{4}⁡4t}\,i+\frac{4{e}^{2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡4t}{1+4{e}^{4t}\sin^{4}⁡4t}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{2t})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡4t)\,j \\  & =2{e}^{2t}\,i+4\operatorname{cos}⁡4t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =(\frac{2\sin^{2}⁡4t}{1+4{e}^{4t}\sin^{4}⁡4t}\,i+\frac{4{e}^{2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡4t}{1+4{e}^{4t}\sin^{4}⁡4t}\,j)\cdot (2{e}^{2t}\,i+4\operatorname{cos}⁡4t\,j) \\  & =\frac{4{e}^{2t}\sin^{2}⁡4t}{1+4{e}^{4t}\sin^{4}⁡4t}+\frac{16{e}^{2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡4t\operatorname{cos}⁡4t}{1+4{e}^{4t}\sin^{4}⁡4t} \\  & =\frac{2{e}^{2t}(2\sin^{2}⁡4t+8\operatorname{sin}⁡4t\operatorname{cos}⁡4t)}{1+4{e}^{4t}\sin^{4}⁡4t}.\end{aligned}
$$
